The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) High Court in Zuba, Abuja, on Friday sentenced two persons to death by hanging for the murder of a National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) member in 2022.
​The International Centre for Investigative Reporting ( ICIR ) reported that Jennifer Tsembe and Solomon Abuh were convicted and sentenced for the death of Stephanie Terungwa, aged 26.
​Meanwhile, the court also sentenced the third defendant, Monday Simon, to 14 years’ imprisonment for conspiracy and abduction of Ms Terungwa.
​Since 2022, the Nigeria Police Force (NPF) has been prosecuting the trio after Ms Terungwa was reported missing in Abuja.
​Ms Terungwa’s remains were later found. The convicts who were arrested by the police confessed their involvement in her death.
Ms Tsembe confessed to luring the deceased to her residence in Maitama, tying her up and pouring acid on the victim.

Ms Tsembe cited jealousy over Ms Terungwa having a child with her boyfriend as a motivation.
During the proceedings, the prosecution lawyer, Adama Musa, presented nine witnesses and 15 exhibits to prove his case.
Following a four-year trial, the judge found the trio guilty of the crime and convicted them.
​Ahmed Sanusi, the Commissioner of Police in the FCT, lauded the investigating team and legal unit for their effort, a police statement said.
This sentence comes amidst demands by right groups to revoke the death penalty.
On 9 October, the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), Avocats Sans Frontieres, the Australian High Commission, the Embassy of the Federal Republic of Germany and the Spanish embassy in Nigeria called for the revocation of the death penalty in Nigeria.
By December, Nigeria would mark 10 consecutive years without a state execution, meeting the international standard for a de facto moratorium. However, over 3,000 persons are on prolonged death row detention.
Amnesty International reported that as of 2025, 145 countries have abolished the death penalty both in law and practice.
While Nigeria would become a de facto abolitionist state, by December, some laws allow for state pardon for those on death row.
Similarly, section 12(2)(c) of the Nigerian Correctional Service (NCoS) Act, 2019 allows the commutation of a death sentence to life imprisonment under specific conditions.
